stem:
Leela blows air into a rubber balloon. The balloon swells and becomes firm on every side she touches.

She asks what this shows about the pressure of the air inside.

options.text: The air pushes only downward on the bottom of the balloon.
The air also pushes outward on the side walls of the balloon.
The balloon swells only because rubber is stretchy, not because air pushes on the walls.
Air pressure acts on the walls only where Leela's fingers touch.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Air inside pushes outward on the balloon walls in all directions, so the balloon firms up on the sides as well as at the bottom.

teacher.key_rationale: Gases exert pressure on the walls of their containers in all directions, not only downward or only at touch points.
